title: Final Whistle
intro: For the hour after a match, when the score is settled but you are still wired. Adrenaline does not switch off just because you sat down.

Move first to bleed it off, get your legs above your heart, then breathe. Box breathing comes before the long exhale on purpose: a head still going over points needs something to hold on to before it will drop.

exercises.name: Easy Walk
exercises.note: Five minutes of easy movement first is what makes the rest of this land.

good: Slow walk anywhere, around the court is fine
Let your breathing come down on its own
bad: Sitting straight down with your bag

good: Swing the arm across the body and back open, relaxed
Let the upper back turn with it
Move slowly between the two shapes
Breathe with it, out as you round

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall
exercises.note: Feet above the heart is what helps heavy legs drain after a long match.

good: Heels resting up the wall, arms out wide
Let the legs be heavy and the floor take you
Knees wide, hips back to the heels, arms long
Breathe into your back and feel it widen
bad: Rushing to get to the breathing

exercises.name: Box Breathing
exercises.note: The counting is the point: it gives a racing head something to hold on to.

good: In for four, hold four, out for four, hold four
Nose breathing the whole way if you can
bad: Straining the holds — drop to three counts if four is a fight

exercises.name: Extended Exhale Breathing
exercises.note: The long out-breath is the part that does the work.

good: In through the nose for four, out through the mouth for eight
Only the hand on your belly should move
bad: Rushing the exhale to get to the next breath
